newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber ends mixed despite China inquiries.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber ends mixed despite China inquiries.

text.p: The Malaysian rubber market was mixed in slow trading despite some inquiries from China on SMR grades of rubber, dealers said.
"Our SMR grades rubber are much lower than other producing countries. We see some inquiries coming in from China," a dealer at a trading firm said. "They are just checking on the levels."
Trading houses offered SMR CV at 326 cents, SMR L at 305, SMR 10 at 255 and drum latex at 224.
However, the dealer said there was still no keen incentive dealing interest from Europe.
Dealers said lower Tokyo prices because of a stronger Japanese yen also caused cautioness among buyers.
At the close, June RSS Ones buyer rose a cent to 270.50 cents ($1.08) a kg but June SMR 20 buyer was down half a cent at 254.50 cents.
The INRO five-day average was 207.62 Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg on May 9 from 207.91 on May 8.
The daily indicator was 207.10 against 207.77. -- Tan Lee Lee (603-230-7510) ($1=2.5060 ringgit)
